hints: Find the positions of the quartiles: Q1 at cumulative frequency 120 / 4 = 30 and Q3 at cumulative frequency 3 * 120 / 4 = 90.
Read the horizontal time values corresponding to cumulative frequencies 30 and 90 from the graph.
Subtract Q1 from Q3 to estimate the interquartile range: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 53 - 35.5 = 17.5 seconds.
walkthrough:
Determine the cumulative frequency levels corresponding to the lower and upper quartiles for $N = 120$:
$$\text{Level of } Q_1 = 0.25 \times 120 = 30$$
$$\text{Level of } Q_3 = 0.75 \times 120 = 90$$

Read the estimated quartiles from the cumulative frequency graph:
$$Q_1 \approx 35.5\text{ seconds} \quad (35 \le Q_1 \le 36)$$
$$Q_3 \approx 53\text{ seconds} \quad (52 \le Q_3 \le 54)$$

Calculate the estimated interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 53 - 35.5 = 17.5\text{ seconds} \quad (16 \le \operatorname{IQR} \le 19)$$

ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Reads Q1 from CF = 30 and Q3 from CF = 90, calculating IQR = Q3 - Q1 between 16 and 19 seconds.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the total frequency:
The cumulative frequency curve reaches a total of $N = 120$ children.

Step 2: Find the vertical positions of the lower quartile $Q_1$ and upper quartile $Q_3$:
- Lower quartile rank:
$$\frac{1}{4} N = \frac{120}{4} = 30$$
- Upper quartile rank:
$$\frac{3}{4} N = \frac{3 \times 120}{4} = 90$$

Step 3: Read the horizontal axis values corresponding to these ranks:
- At cumulative frequency $30$, trace across to the curve and down to the horizontal axis to read $Q_1 \approx 35.5$ seconds (acceptable range: $35$ to $36$).
- At cumulative frequency $90$, trace across to the curve and down to the horizontal axis to read $Q_3 \approx 53$ seconds (acceptable range: $52$ to $54$).

Step 4: Compute the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 53 - 35.5 = 17.5\text{ seconds}$$
(Any value in the range $16$ to $19$ seconds is accepted).

hints: If 35% took longer than T seconds, then 100% - 35% = 65% took T seconds or less.
Locate 78 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and read the corresponding time T on the horizontal axis: T is approximately 49 seconds.
walkthrough:
Determine the number of children taking less than or equal to $T$ seconds:
$$\text{Percentage} = 100\% - 35\% = 65\%$$
$$\text{Cumulative frequency} = 0.65 \times 120 = 78$$

Read the value of $T$ from the graph at cumulative frequency $78$:
$$T \approx 49\text{ seconds} \quad (48 \le T \le 50)$$

ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Identifies CF level 120 - 42 = 78 and reads T between 48 and 50 seconds.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Convert the upper tail condition to a cumulative (lower tail) frequency:
We are told that $35\%$ of the children took longer than $T$ seconds.
Therefore, the remaining percentage took at most $T$ seconds:
$$100\% - 35\% = 65\%$$

Step 2: Calculate the cumulative frequency value:
$$\text{Cumulative frequency} = 65\% \times 120 = \frac{65}{100} \times 120 = 78$$
(Alternatively, $120 - (0.35 \times 120) = 120 - 42 = 78$.)

Step 3: Read the time value $T$ from the graph:
Locate $78$ on the vertical axis, trace horizontally to the curve, and drop down to read the time on the horizontal axis:
$$T \approx 49\text{ seconds}$$
(Any reading between $48$ and $50$ seconds is acceptable).
